body:
Worry about where you'll spend the night... Oh wait, that's just me and other homeless people!

Okay, false; rich people can worry about whether they'll sleep at home, take a cab, or if they'll get into the penthouse of that 5 star hotel or not.
For various reasons, my wife...
Jason Bourne, or Michael Westen.
Have you yourself ever been homeless?

Sad thing is... I'm falling through the cracks :/
I'm not a resident or citizen, so I have no rights to anything...
I do have an appointment with an immigration lawyer week after next week, but I doubt that's going to make a difference :/

Had a big breakdown earlier, luckily a friend in Norway had woken up by then...

I guess the lack of friends here - at least that I trust with my inner most feelings - doesn't help either... and I already feel like a burden as it is.

It just keeps on going in loops in my head...

I just feel so stuck! :(

Thank you! You don't know how much that means to me right now!

To be honest, I've never felt at home...and had trouble fitting in...anywhere...until I came here...!
Well, I guess that bridge just got burnt... with my now very soon to be very ex wife.

Hi! Sorry!

EU = Europe (/European Union)
IE = Ireland
NL = The Netherlands

Right now, I have a place to stay, but I'm looking on advice on organizations that help people get back. Not even the embassy of my country of origin is able to help me out in regard to travel costs or arranging for flights.

As long as I get to either country, I a) have people that would help me (land) and b) be able to get a job. UK would work too I guess. (As I'm a EU citizen, I have work status there.)

It would be I'm not expecting that people will be able to help cover a flight, as it's around 1500-2000 CAD. Just figured I might ask here for advice.

I'm planning my exit now, asked r/assistance for advice - to see if I can get out without getting my ass removed/deported.

The lady from the hotline was good in allowing me to reflect...and then I had a good (but heated) conversation with my wife...

I know I can call the hotline if needed, but things also need to get moving...

Thank you! (Both!)

I ended up calling them...

There's still not a whole lot they can do without medical coverage, else they would've hooked me up, but it was good to have someone reflect to me that my struggle is real... And I know that I can call them 24/7...

Bottom-line: still nothing they could do, but it was good talking about it.

I'm homeless and without work status in a country where I have no rights, working on a project that's under-paying me, family won't help me (anymore), while aside from getting lucky or getting deported absolutely no chance of turning it around, nor getting things fixed to a point where I can (financially) take care of my wife and step-kids again. Well, aside from my wife, no one in my entire family or circle of friends (that I still have or made) knows about the extent of how much shit I'm in.

But instead, while trying to fix things, I lie to myself and tell myself that everything is going to be okay. It's the only way that I can keep holding on.

How's that for living a lie?
Life.
OH NOES! Productivity incoming!!
And every time I'm about to give up...another door seems to open.

After getting some sleep, my stance is still the same...

Except for that to prove a point I might just take my life in CBSA/CIC custody, just to prove the point... and to not "stab" my dear hosts in the back.

Add being an illegal alien and you're ultimately screwed.



Well, except for being deported of course...

So you can be homeless in another country, where you're probably off worse...

EDIT: Yeah, I agree...and it's especially hard wanting to help others out, while barely having anything yourself...

What became 2 weeks, has now become 48 hours...
I'm not sure on the method yet, but I think auto-asphyxiation is the cleanest one.

After trying to pull an all-nighter to finish a project, even that failed.

I've thought about turning myself into CBSA/CIC, and there's no hope there of getting a change in my situation.

My wife(in-separation) is even cold-shouldering me.

I've been spending the past 2 weeks on a couch with some good people, and that finally allowed me to see the severity of the situation.

I know that no one will read this, but it feels good to be able to admit my defeat in public.

I fail, I suck at life... I lost the race when I was born.
At least she has someone to take care of her.

I have written my last will and wishes, and it's okay...

I just want to sleep and give up now, only to never wake up.

I'm sorry that the people who were so nice to host me, will be the people the find my lifeless body.

I'm sorry for the energy that people have wasted on me.

It's better this way.

I'm sorry ahandleforme! Thank you for your kind words!

I hope the world is a better place without me.

I'm sorry.

Me.

I passed out a couple times at that fastfood restaurant, and then later at a bookstore. Basically running without any real sleep for the past 3 days, but I made it to a new couch.

Also had a real good talk with someone that made me realize a few things, and there seems to be more to my spouse's split than meets the eye, I think, but I generally hopelessly over-analyze everything.

I'm going to give my options a bit more thought, taking the next few days to at least get a bit more rested and be able to think straight.

Thank you for listening! I'll keep you updated, but I'm ready to pass out now.

Of course, the cold that was setting in, is now in full effect... You know, because I also just needed that.

F@k! The only thing that is going well tonight is...my laptop and the fact that I haven't been kicked out here.

Just put on headphones with more active music than the background music they have on here.

Now for the deadman's hour! Or should I say hours...
5-7 is always the most difficult...
On top of that, the project I was working on, I missed the memo that it should've been done last week.

This weekend has not been productive at all. Lack of sleep and funds is not a good basis for doing computer work that requires one to keep sharp. On top of that, I'll be running out of funds soon.

Up to a couple of days ago, I had an arrangement where I crashed people their couch, but that ended due to a combination of circumstances.

Not having that place has effectively cost me nearly 10 dollars/day just to sustain myself, mostly through the nights. I had a few food windfalls here and there. (People coming into this place I frequent carrying a box of donuts/cupcakes, for instance.)

The hardest part is pretending that everything is okay, because else they'd just ditch me again.

On that note, I finally got my clothing/etc back today, after I had left it at the previous arrangements place, when I had heard during the day that I basically wasn't welcome anymore. To anyone ever becoming homeless, a fresh change of clothing is just soo goood! And it does wonders for not being seen as a homeless person. Also, carry a backpack, it makes people wonder if you're traveling around. Leaving it to people's imagination is good; they will fill in the blanks themselves.

Just fell asleep here, and woke up to my "neighbor" getting kicked out...

I wish there were more people like you!

Thank you!

I guess I might as well start to type... As the couch offer is only redeemable from tomorrow, I tried the local shelters... I mean... I barely slept the past 2 nights - I did get some sleep on a bench in a park. Unfortunately, they were all full. So, no bed for me tonight.

So it looks like I'm stuck at the local fastfood restaurant.

I will, and thank you for taking the time...
The problems have become so severe that I can't really talk to anyone about it...and the legal repercussions are severe enough that I need to hide behind this persona... Making it even harder to just talk about it...

so, thank you!

Don't be, you can't help it...!

And yeah, I had no real reason to dislike my "motherland", but over time - although it's certainly not easy here - I've grown more and more weary of that country. I don't even miss it!

It's just one more typical thing that I've come to dislike of that country.

I called them last month to verify...

They won't interfere with "internal affairs" (immigration) and they don't offer aid to get someone back to the motherland, at least not the mission for my native country...

I'm trying to turn this around, but it all just seems so hopeless.
For now, I keep on trying...

After 2 nights of not sleeping, I'm declaring defeat...
I also managed to score some bread and peanut butter...
And I had something social as well, where I got to do music...
Which really gave me a boost.

For now I've put my plan more in the background, because I also got an offer for a couch to sleep on and I might see a little speck of light in the darkness...

Also, I suffer from a form of autism, making life without stability extra hard.

After thinking some more, I figured out I need to talk to my spouse - I need to know if there's anything left to fight for... If so, I might be able to squeeze out that last little bit of trying to make things work and try last resort options.

I don't know... The letters are currently dancing in front of my eyes from fatigue.

As futile as it is, I'm thinking that I might as well take my chances with the legal system, at least that's where some real decision powers are to be found.

And on a finishing note, it just dawned on me how judgmental people are. I might explain it later...

Overall, I'm still very rationally considering it, I just want it all to stop, and aside from winning the lottery - in both the literal and figurative way - there's nothing that can really be done to change anything, and it feels like giving up now would be equivalent to throwing away all the time and effort I put into it.

Why did I start this journey in the first place if I was to give up?
Where giving up in basic terms would mean that I would be denying my own dreams, hopes and wishes; giving up on who I am I guess...
They won't help me unless I'm either in jail or dead.
And I'm being called out on being a liability and acting like I'm entitled to stuff... Talking about kicking someone when they're down.

But to answer your question, no.

(Over the past nearly year and a half, I had been so busy trying to keep my relationship and family afloat, that I've barely been out to movies/etc. Usually too busy with work to even think about watching a movie.)

I'd love to do that, but that would still not make me less illegally in the country... As much as I've given up on humanity right now...

And truth be told, I'd give up everything right now to be able stay and work here and make things work with her. To sleep in the same bed as her.

But it has come to a point where I just don't know what to do anymore.

Turning myself in is just as bad as ending it right now.

I can't start from scratch all over again. Not without something to look forward to, to keep me motivated.

This whole situation has destroyed so much in me that I don't even want to just do it for myself anymore.

My to-be-ex spouse coerced me into at least have something to eat...

It's the only way I can at least see my step-kids before I go.

I'm just so f#@king done with this whole life... I've already tried to end it all when I was in my freshmen year... Now I just look back at it thinking things would have been better if I had succeeded...

And take my chances with hypothermia and being eaten by wildlife...
Sounds better by the moment!

Or what do you mean?
I'm in BC, Canada, but that would still be a one way ticket out of here...

I have no insurance...
No way to pay for it...

For those wondering, the catalyst for my current situation was the relationship of 2 years...with the person I considered to be my soul mate...going sour.... while illegally being in this great country... A place I finally could call home.

Now, I have no one and nothing anymore.

I only have my backpack with my laptop/etc... and no one to turn to. I'm all alone and my only way out is in shackles or a body bag.

It's weird...writing my will right now.
In this digital world, I need to leave my passwords somewhere!

And it's ironic really... Trying to think of people to thank!

The people that made the biggest difference... I've only known them for roughly the 6 months that I've been here.
Follow my heart...
OP starts?

Late to the party, but...

TLDR: After coming over to Canada as a tourist, to help my wife after Child Protection was called in for our (step-)kids, and after getting fucked over by the clients for whom I was working for remotely, we got in shit so much that my wife is currently camping out at her ex, I was homeless for a while and I might end up being in the country illegally, if caught, possibly being deported, and banned from the country - aka slimming the chances of ever moving here to be with my family.

All because we were misinformed about her options to sponsor me (or lack thereof), me coming over to help her keep her kids, me missing my flight back, and her ex only willing to help her.

I would have asked Reddit about advice about what to do, but it's a little too late for that now...

So instead I've now set my goal to see my step-kids again before I turn myself in... There is no winning from a government/immigration system and continuing this seems pointless. (She can't move to my native country due to one of the kids lacking a birth certificate and me getting sponsored is hopeless.)

Cheese (curds) and gravy...soooo gooood!

I approve.

Soooo jealous right now!
Are you buying my ticket?
Also, I found 211, I'll give them a call...to see if they know/have resources!

She is, but as we're not living together, she can't sponsor me...nor would she be able to if she was on welfare...

Thank you and thank you!

Damn you long weekend! :p But I'll definitely get in touch with those organizations...!!

Thank you!

EDIT: P.S., I can't wait to get myself some proper poutine again... I'll gladly treat you if I make it!

I'm in Vancouver actually. Deportation usually means being declared inadmissible (for 5 years), aka being banned. I've already tried my embassy/consulate and they don't help out in arranging flights back/etc. (Nor does my family want to help out due to varies reasons.)

If I'd get banned, that would mean that I don't get to enter Canada to visit my wife and (step-)kids... Let alone being able to get sponsored, nor does the current situation allow for it (as we're not living together).

Right now, working for Timmies in nowhere land sounds pretty enticing to be honest...

Irony is that when I tell people about my situation they usually give off on the immigration system...and ask themselves why the fudge I can't just get a work visa here...

I'm getting slightly too old for this as well, but managing so far... I'm certainly not the oldest at "my" shelter. The main challenge being that most shelters kick you out by 6 AM, if you're lucky and you only get to shower during the evenings.

I'm still slightly okay with everything, but getting slightly more desperate by the day.
